status_summary: The America First Trade Policy memorandum of 2025-01-20 assigned trade reviews to USTR, Commerce, Treasury and OMB rather than naming USTR the single lead. USTR's FY2027 budget justification (cover dated March 2026) requests 95 million dollars and 301 FTE for Salaries and Expenses, against 65 million dollars and 230 FTE enacted for that account in FY2026; counting the Trade Enforcement Trust Fund, the document describes the increase as 7 million dollars and 27 FTE. On advisory committees, USTR published notices on 2026-03-04 and 2026-03-12 continuing the main committees for new four-year terms, with ability to advance the America First Trade Policy listed as a selection factor, so the legacy committees were continued with changed criteria rather than disposed of.

timeline.event: The President signed the America First Trade Policy memorandum, assigning separate trade reviews to USTR, Commerce and Treasury, with reports due by 2025-04-01 (published 2025-01-30).
USTR published a notice continuing the Advisory Committee for Trade Policy and Negotiations and seeking nominations, listing ability to advance America First Trade Policy among selection factors.
USTR and Commerce published a notice continuing the Industry Trade Advisory Committees (15 committees plus a chairs committee) and seeking applications.
USTR's FY2027 budget justification (cover dated March 2026) requested 95 million dollars and 301 FTE for Salaries and Expenses, up from 65 million dollars and 230 FTE enacted for FY2026.

title: Empower USTR to lead trade policy and dispose of legacy advisory committees
uncertainties: The budget justification's cover gives only March 2026, so the day in its date is approximate. The charters for the industry committees were reported as signed in July 2026 but are not cited as events. Whether USTR or White House economic staff led tariff decisions in practice was not resolved; the January 2025 memorandum splits reviews among several offices. FY2027 appropriations status was not checked. The progress figure is an inference. Leadership of trade agreements is also covered by c26-05.
